title: 'Time traveller' returned from 2036 to warn humanity about nuclear war
excerpt: John Titor claimed to be a time traveller from the year 2036 who had come back to the year 2000 to warn of nuclear war and the rise of a despotic regime
content:
John Titor claimed to be a time traveller from the year 2036 who had come back to the year 2000 to warn of nuclear war and the rise of a despotic regime

07:30, 26 Sep 2026Updated 07:49, 26 Sep 2026

It may sound like the plot of a science fiction film, but some are convinced the mysterious John Titor genuinely travelled back to the year 2000 to warn us of a bleak future for mankind. Emerging on an internet forum, Titor made bold claims about his mission to divert humanity from a fate riddled with nuclear warfare and tyrannical governments.

‌

To this day, conspiracy enthusiasts regard the figure of Titor with reverence, many expressing belief in his remarkable claims of time travel. After posting several predictions about the future, offering advice on how to evade disaster, and sharing images of what he claimed was his time machine, he abruptly disappeared.

‌

On November 2, 2000, he posted online: "Greetings. I am a time traveller from the year 2036. I am on my way home after getting an IBM 5100 computer system from the year 1975."

‌

His online activity was peppered with foreboding predictions, guidance on avoiding worldwide catastrophe, and images of what he claimed was his time-travelling device - a machine strikingly similar to the iconic DeLorean from "Back to the Future".

"None of the things I have said will be a surprise. They were set in motion 10, 20, even 30 years ago," Titor claimed.

"Are you really surprised to find out that Iraq has nukes now or is that just BS to whip everyone up into accepting the next war?".

Titor insisted he was part of a military unit from the future stationed in Florida, travelling back to 1975 but making a pit stop in 2000 for "personal reasons."

He shocked online users by saying: "My goal is not to be believed. Perhaps I should let you all in on a little secret. No one likes you in the future. This time period is looked at as being full of lazy, self-centered, civically ignorant sheep.

‌

"Perhaps you should be less concerned about me and more concerned about that."

However, Titor then made a remarkable series of forecasts which, over time, have either materialised or contained grains of truth.

‌

In one forecast, Titor discussed the deception surrounding weapons of mass destruction prior to the Iraq War in 2003.

Many suspect that claims about WMDs in Saddam Hussein's arsenal were just a pretext to justify military action against the Middle Eastern nation, and some believe this prediction demonstrates Titor possessed advance knowledge of the conflict.

Another extraordinary forecast concerned one of the earliest personal computers, the IBM 5100, which harboured a secret capability only disclosed in August 2004.

‌

This feature enabled the device to simulate programmes in legacy languages utilised by IBM mainframes, though the corporation hid this functionality to prevent exploitation by rivals.

Yet in 2001, Titor had written: "You mean other than the mad cow pandemic, the breakthroughs in high-energy physics and the unknown functions of the 5100?" In 2004, three years after Titor disappeared from the internet, IBM revealed that such a secret function did indeed exist.

‌

This remarkable revelation rekindled speculation that John Titor either possessed extensive knowledge of IBM programming, or was genuinely a time traveller.

In one of Titor's messages, he casually posed the question: "Care to share with me how you solved the overheating problem on your space plane?".

‌

Many believe Titor was hinting at the Columbia space shuttle tragedy in 2003, which claimed the lives of all seven crew members. Disaster struck when a piece of foam hit the shuttle's wing during launch, causing superheated air to penetrate the damaged wing during re-entry and destroy the craft.

Conspiracy theorists argue this represents further evidence that Titor foresaw the fate of the NASA mission. Some of John Titor's forecasts never materialised, such as his prediction of Civil War erupting in America from 2004.

He also foresaw mad cow disease spreading globally and the Olympics being scrapped. Despite these unfulfilled prophecies, conspiracy theorists maintain that he prevented these events simply by alerting us to them.

‌

Titor explained that by existing in the past, he was generating an alternative timeline where certain aspects of his reality differed from ours. He wrote: "News events that happen at different times, football games won by other teams, things like that."

In 2009, a private investigator pointed the finger at Larry Haber, a Florida-based solicitor, and his computer scientist brother John Rick Haber as the most probable people behind the myth.

Both men had the necessary tech-savvy, and it was revealed that Haber was the CEO of a profit-making company named the John Titor Foundation, established two years after Titor's online emergence.

Despite this, several dedicated fans continue to insist that Titor's forecasts of future events were too intricate to be fabricated.

Even now, those who interacted with him remain curious about his identity and whether his tale of time travel held any truth.
